case.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case.limits: The camera captured a scene a human staged in full. A generative model contributes expressive choices of its own, and how much human selection is enough is exactly what the Copyright Office and the courts are now drawing case by case.
case.holding: A photograph can be copyrighted because the photographer's choices of pose, lighting, arrangement and expression make the human, not the camera, the author of the work.

live_cases.name: University of Tennessee Research Foundation v. Anthropic PBC

case.why_ai_cites_it: The first machine-authorship case, and the template both sides use. AI companies and their users cite it for the claim that prompting, curating and arranging make a human the author of machine-assisted output; opponents cite it for the premise that authorship requires a human making the creative choices at all.
